tokyo_shark_coffee.price_note: SHARK COFFEE PUBLISHES ITS WHOLE IN-STORE CARD AS STRUCTURED TEXT, WITH A GLUTEN-FREE AND A VEGAN BADGE PRINTED AGAINST EVERY ITEM THAT EARNS ONE — this is one of the most legible coeliac and vegan menus in Shibuya and the badges below are the shop's own, not an inference. The bakery counter is roughly half rice-flour, and almost every sweet carries BOTH badges. ⚠ THE ONE REAL TRAP IS THE OAT MILK. Every latte can be switched to organic oat, rice or almond milk for +80円, and the two chai lattes are built on organic oat milk as standard — but the shop badges those chai lattes VEGAN, not gluten-free, and it is right not to. Oats are not wheat, but Japanese oat milk is not certified gluten-free and oat crops are routinely wheat-contaminated; a coeliac ordering a plant-milk latte here should take the rice or almond option, which is the same +80円. ⚠ THE SECOND TRAP IS THAT GF AND VEGAN ARE NOT THE SAME BADGE. 米粉あんバター is gluten-free and contains butter; ２種のチーズピザ and デリフォカッチャ（オニオンベーコン） are gluten-free and contain cheese and bacon; the scones, チョコツイスト, 腹黒メロンパン, クルミのシナモンロール and 焼きカレーパン are vegan wheat bakes and are exactly what a coeliac must not order. ⚠ 十割そば粉のガトーショコラ is badged gluten-free and is genuinely 100% buckwheat flour — the rare case where 十割 means what a coeliac hopes it means, because it is a baked cake and not soba, so there is no 打ち粉 and no shared noodle water. Items where the shop prints 「Gluten-Freeに変更可」 (the two Greek yogurts and the kids' set) are recorded ask, because the GF version is a swap you have to request. Cakes carrying only the Vegan badge — ヴィーガンキャロットケーキ, ヴィーガンレモンケーキ — are recorded ask on gluten rather than no: the shop labels GF everywhere else, so the absence of the badge is meaningful, but it does not by itself say wheat. The page warns 「商品は売り切れている場合もございます。店内レジ前メニュー、ショーケースをご確認ください。」 — the case sells out, so treat this as the full range rather than today's stock. Prices are as printed, tax included. A dog menu exists on a separate page and is not recorded here.

tokyo_yinega_yinega.price_note: YINEGA PUBLISHES ITS WHOLE CARD WITH PRICES IN ENGLISH, ORGANISED AS AFRICAN / ETHNIC / EUROPEAN / VEGETARIAN — and the VEGETARIAN heading is the shop's own, which is rare in Shibuya and is the reason this record matters. ⚠ BUT READ THE VEGETARIAN SECTION AS 'VEGETARIAN', NOT 'VEGAN', BECAUSE THE SHOP MEANS IT LITERALLY: falafel plate arrives with a yogurt sauce, Brick is a fried roll of potato, TUNA and egg, salmon and vegetable shawarma is smoked salmon, potato and green beans comes with anchovy mayonnaise, and Gorgonzola potato gratin is cheese. Of the eight things printed under VEGETARIAN, only Khums (hummus) and Mushroom Ajillo are plausibly vegan, and Veggie rice bowl is stir-fried with Thai herbs, which in practice usually means fish sauce. ⚠ THE ONE OUTSTANDING GLUTEN FACT ON THIS MENU IS THAT THE SHOP TELLS YOU ITSELF. Under the African main dish it describes couscous as 'The world's smallest granular pasta made from wheat flour' — a first-party statement that the couscous is wheat, which is worth more than any inference. The African main dish at ¥1200 is a build: you pick one of five sauces and one of three staples, and the staple is where the whole gluten question sits. Rice and Fufu (yam, +¥300) are naturally gluten-free starches; couscous is not. That makes a sauce-plus-rice or sauce-plus-fufu plate the most promising coeliac order in the building, though none of the five sauces is described ingredient-by-ingredient, so every one is recorded ask rather than gf. The lunch menu runs 11:30–16:00 from ¥1000 with salad and soup, and the daily special rotates through a list the shop prints (Spicy Indian Curry / Sandwich / Vegetarian bowl / Shawarma / Mafe / Taco rice / Thai fried chicken / Omurice / Yassa) — those are named without prices and are recorded as a single lunch line rather than invented as items. Several sections end 'and More...', so this is the published card, not necessarily the full board.

tokyo_banh_xeo_saigon_shinjuku.price_note: THE SHOP'S OWN SITE HAS NO MENU PAGE — the navigation is TOP / ご予約 / こだわり / バインセオ物語 / 新着情報 / アクセス and nothing else, and the /menu path does not exist. Everything recorded below comes from the shop's own 新着情報 posts, which is why this record is partial rather than authoritative: the posts name dishes and give course and campaign prices, but the à-la-carte card is not published anywhere the shop controls. ⚠ THIS IS A HIGH-VALUE COELIAC ADDRESS AND THE RECORD SHOULD BE FINISHED WHEN A REAL MENU SURFACES, because the house dish is bánh xèo, whose batter is rice flour and turmeric with no wheat in the traditional recipe, and the lunch line-up the shop lists is bún bò Huế, cơm tấm, phở, hủ tiếu and hủ tiếu khô — rice noodles and rice, top to bottom, with not a wheat noodle among them. ⚠ WHAT STOPS ANY OF IT BEING RECORDED GF IS THE SAUCE. The shop's own seasonal post describes its nước chấm as 「特製のヌクチャム(ベトナム豆醤油)タレ」 — it calls its own dipping sauce a Vietnamese SOY sauce, and a soy-based dressing is a wheat question until someone reads the bottle. That is also a vegan fact: nước chấm is normally built on fish sauce, and the phở and bún bò Huế broths are meat. Nothing here is recorded vegan. The 444円 bánh xèo runs only on weekday dates containing a 4, one per customer, at 488円 including tax — the shop prints both the pre-tax and tax-included figure, which is unusual and is recorded as printed. Weekday lunch now runs to 16:00 with a happy hour on drinks.

tokyo_shiraiwa_asakusa_ten.price_note: THRIVE COMPANY'S BRAND PAGE FOR しらいわ 浅草店 IS LIVE AND CARRIES NO MENU AND NO PRICES. It was fetched and read in full: it gives the address (浅草1-30-5 スズヤビル 1F, on 新仲見世商店街), the phone number, 39 seats, opening hours and one paragraph of description, and that paragraph is the only thing on the page with food content — 「伝統的な味わいのお好み焼き、多彩な具材で楽しめるもんじゃ焼き、新鮮な食材を使用した鉄板焼き」. There is no /menu path under the brand and no PDF; the page's only outbound food link is Tabelog, which 403s from this egress. ⚠ FOR A COELIAC THE DESCRIPTION ALONE IS DECISIVE AND NEGATIVE. This is a 鉄板焼き専門店 whose two named specialities are okonomiyaki and monjayaki. Okonomiyaki batter is wheat flour; monja is a thinner wheat batter cooked directly on the same griddle that everything else on the menu touches, so even a plain grilled item is cooked in wheat. A shared teppan is the single worst cross-contact surface in Japanese dining and there is no version of this room that works without the shop's cooperation. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN it is equally unpromising: okonomiyaki batter is bound with egg and stocked with dashi, and the standard toppings are katsuobushi and mayonnaise. No item is recorded because the shop publishes no item — the three dish types below are the categories the brand page itself names, priced nowhere.

tokyo_juwari_soba_sagatani_shi_2.price_note: THE OPERATOR'S OWN PAGE FOR THIS BRANCH PUBLISHES NO MENU AND SAYS SO: its 「メニューを確認」 button is footnoted 「※「メニューを確認」は外部グルメポータルにリンクしております」 and points at Tabelog, which 403s from this egress. What the page does give is first-party and worth having: the branch is 新宿区西新宿1-1 京王モール B-4区画, open 7:00–22:00 every day, 19 counter seats plus 5 standing, average spend 〜999円, cash not accepted by card but e-money and QR accepted. ⚠ THE SOBA AND TSUYU DETAIL IS THE PART A COELIAC NEEDS AND IT IS ALL BAD NEWS DRESSED AS GOOD. The brand name is 十割蕎麦 — 100% buckwheat, milled in-store on a stone mill, with the water content adjusted daily. That sounds like the one soba a coeliac could eat, and it is not: 十割 describes the dough, not the kitchen. The 打ち粉 dusting flour used to stop 100% buckwheat dough tearing is conventionally wheat, the noodles are boiled in water shared with everything else at a 7am-to-10pm standing counter, and this branch also runs a tempura fryer — the brand advertises 「挽きたて・打ちたて・茹でたて・揚げたて」, and 揚げたて is freshly fried tempura in wheat batter over the same counter. ⚠ THE TSUYU IS BOTH A GLUTEN FACT AND A VEGAN FACT. The shop describes its cold tsuyu as 昆布 plus three blended 節 and its hot tsuyu as 昆布 plus four blended 節 — katsuobushi and its relatives are fish, so no tsuyu here is vegan, and a Japanese noodle tsuyu is built on soy sauce, which is wheat-brewed unless declared tamari. The free wakame at the counter is the one thing on the premises that is plainly plant-based. No priced item is recorded because the operator publishes none.

tokyo_chugoku_saikan_shien.price_note: 志苑'S OWN SITE HAS A 「志苑のごはん」 MENU PAGE AND IT NAMES SIX DISHES AND NO PRICES — two under ＜ランチ＞ and four under ＜ディナー＞, presented as photographs with captions rather than a priced card. That is the whole of the shop's published food content; there is no PDF, no allergen note and no à-la-carte list, and the dataset's menu_url is Tabelog, which 403s from this egress. ⚠ EVERY ONE OF THE SIX IS A SOY DISH AND NONE OF THEM IS A COELIAC ORDER AS PUBLISHED. 特製焼き餃子 is a wheat wrapper before the sauce is even considered. 志苑特製豚の角煮 and 海老のチリソース and 彩り野菜の黒酢の酢豚 are all built on 醤油 or a soy-and-vinegar sauce, and Chinese black-vinegar sweet-and-sour is normally thickened with starch but seasoned with soy. 特製坦々麺 is a wheat noodle. ⚠ THE ONE LINE WORTH A QUESTION IS 志苑特製土鍋麻婆豆腐. Mapo doufu is the classic almost-there dish: the tofu, the chilli and the Sichuan pepper are all gluten-free, but the 豆板醤 that defines it is a broad-bean paste fermented WITH WHEAT FLOUR in nearly every commercial brand, and restaurant mapo is normally finished with soy sauce and minced pork. It is recorded ask on gluten and no on vegan, and it is the dish to ask about if you are here. Nothing is recorded gf. Prices are unknown for every line.

tokyo_shibuya_sarashina.price_note: THE WEBSITE RECORDED FOR THIS SHOP NO LONGER EXISTS AS A DOMAIN. www.shibuyasarashina.com and the bare shibuyasarashina.com both return NXDOMAIN — 「Non-existent domain」 — from two independent public resolvers (Google 8.8.8.8 and Cloudflare 1.1.1.1). This is not a firewall, a 403 or a timeout; the name has been withdrawn from DNS, so there is no page to fetch and no menu to read, and the dataset's website field should be treated as stale. The only other link on file is Tabelog, which serves a Cloudflare managed challenge to this egress. Nothing about the shop's food is established. ⚠ WORTH RETURNING TO WHEN A LIVE SOURCE APPEARS, and worth flagging what the record already implies in the meantime: 更科 (sarashina) names a specific style of soba made from the pale, refined core of the buckwheat groat, and sarashina flour is so low in the proteins that bind that it is almost always cut with wheat flour to hold the noodle together. A shop trading under 更科 is therefore MORE likely to serve wheat-containing soba than a 十割 house, not less. That is context for the next researcher, not a finding, and no item is recorded.

tokyo_chao_thai_shibuya_dogenz.price_note: CHAOTHAI.JP IS A STUDIO-BUILT SPA AND ITS MENU PAGES RENDER NOTHING TO A FETCHER. The sitemap was read and the four general-branch menu URLs it lists — /menu/grand/general, /menu/lunch/general, /menu/course/general, /menu/drink/general — were each fetched directly and each returned about 38 KB of identical shell markup containing zero prices; the item data is pulled at runtime from api.cms.studiodesignapp.com. A JS-rendering fetch of the grand and lunch pages returned NO ITEMS RENDERED as well. So no priced card exists in any form this machine can read, and that is the finding rather than a gap in effort. ⚠ EVERY DISH NAME BELOW COMES FROM THE SHOP'S OWN SECTION DESCRIPTIONS, WHICH DO SURVIVE IN THE PAGE PAYLOAD, and each is recorded without a price because none is published. Grand menu: 「世界三大スープ「トムヤムクン」や青パパイヤのサラダ「ソムタム」、本格カレーまで」. Lunch: 「メイン料理にタイサラダ・スープ・デザートが付く…30種類以上の豊富なメニューからお選びいただけます」. Course: 「自分好みにカスタマイズできる全5種類のコース料理…プリフィクススタイル」 with nomihodai plans. Drinks: 「シンハーやチャーンなどの定番タイビール…タイ産ワイン「モンスーンヴァレー」や南国フルーツのカクテル」. Branch facts are first-party: 渋谷区道玄坂2-9-10 K&Kビル 2F, weekday lunch 11:30–15:00 (L.O.14:30) and dinner 17:00–23:00 (L.O.22:00), weekends 11:30–23:00, no closing day, budget 2,000–3,000円, cash and cards but no e-money, and the chain is Thai-Embassy-certified with a Thai head chef. ⚠ THAI FOOD IS THE BEST STRUCTURAL BET IN THIS DATASET AND THE WORST DOCUMENTED. Thai cooking is rice-noodle and rice based and uses fish sauce rather than soy as its default salt, which is why a Thai kitchen so often has genuinely gluten-free dishes — but it is fish sauce, so almost nothing is vegan, and oyster sauce and soy do appear in stir-fries. Nothing here can be recorded gf or vegan on a description alone; the four dishes below are recorded ask/no and this record should be finished the moment a readable card appears.

tokyo_tori_soba_mitaba.price_note: ⚠ THE MENU BELOW IS USER-SUBMITTED, NOT THE SHOP’S OWN BOARD. Yahoo! Map heads this list ユーザー投稿のメニュー — items typed in by members of the public — and prints its own disclaimer, ※ 掲載時点の情報です。最新情報は店舗でご確認ください. Nothing here is dated, and the transliterations are diners’ own. In this case the list discredits itself helpfully: two of its entries — 豚ミンチ 238円 and 中華名菜酢豚 213円 — are supermarket packets, not dishes from a Kabukichō ramen counter, and they are proof that anyone can add anything. Several bowls also appear twice under different diners’ names (濃厚鶏つけそば/塩(味玉付) 930円 and 漬けそば 全部のせ 1,030円 against 鶏白湯そば全部乗せ 1,030円). What DOES corroborate part of it is the shop’s own favy page, which independently gives 濃厚鶏そば(塩) 味玉入り at 930円 and 生ビール(アサヒ) at 480円, and hours of 11:00〜05:00 seven days a week. Gnavi was read and carries no prices. X (twitter) is the shop’s other channel and serves no menu to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WHAT THE MENU SHAPE TELLS YOU, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH TRUSTING: this is a CHICKEN shop running two broths at once — 鶏白湯 (paitan, the cloudy emulsified one boiled hard from chicken frames and feet until the collagen breaks down) and 鶏清湯/淡麗 (chintan, the clear one). Both are chicken. There is no vegetable bowl. Every noodle in the building is wheat and every tare is soy-based, so nothing here is gluten-free at any setting. ⚠ THE ONE LINE THAT CHANGES THE ANIMAL ANSWER: あご出汁鶏そば. あご is FLYING FISH, dried and used as a dashi base in Kyushu — so that bowl is chicken AND fish, which matters if you avoid one but not the other. 担々麺 adds sesame paste and, conventionally, minced pork. ⚠ AND THE HOURS ARE THE REASON TO KNOW THIS SHOP EXISTS: open until 5am, which in Kabukichō means it is one of the few places serving actual cooking at four in the morning.

items.ja: 濃厚鶏そば（塩）味玉入り
items.en: Rich chicken soba, salt tare, with a seasoned egg — the one bowl the shop itself publishes a price for. Also recorded by diners as 濃厚鶏つけそば/塩(味玉付) at the same 930円
items.note: 鶏白湯＝鶏がら・もみじを長時間炊いた乳化スープ。中華麺＝小麦、味玉＝醤油漬け。Chicken frames and feet boiled to emulsion — poultry, and unusually concentrated poultry. Wheat noodle. The 味玉 is marinated in soy sauce, so the egg is a wheat item too. A 塩 (salt) tare is often assumed to be the wheat-free option and is not: shio tare is built on more than salt and normally includes a soy or fermented element.

items.ja: 鶏白湯そば 全部乗せ
items.en: The paitan bowl with everything on it. Also recorded as 漬けそば 全部のせ at the same price
items.note: Every extra topping at a ramen counter is soy-marinated — chashu, egg, menma. The loaded bowl is the most wheat-exposed order, not the least.

items.en: The special rich chicken paitan — the house version with the full topping set
items.note: Same chicken emulsion, same wheat noodle, more soy-cured toppings.

items.en: Chicken salt soba with an egg added — the lighter clear-broth line rather than the paitan
items.note: 清湯＝澄んだ鶏スープ。A clear chicken broth rather than an emulsified one. Still chicken, still a wheat noodle, still a soy-marinated egg.

items.en: Light-style chicken soba with a seasoned egg — 淡麗 is the word Japanese ramen uses for a broth built for clarity rather than weight
items.note: The clean-tasting bowl, which is not the same as a clean-ingredient bowl: chicken broth, wheat noodle, soy tare, soy-marinated egg.

items.en: Flying-fish-stock chicken soba — the cheapest bowl on the list
items.note: ⚠ あご＝トビウオ。THE BOWL WHOSE NAME HIDES A SECOND ANIMAL. Ago is FLYING FISH, dried and used as a premium dashi base in Kyushu — so this bowl is chicken and fish together, not chicken alone. Anyone avoiding fish specifically needs to know that, and the English word “chicken soba” will not tell them. Wheat noodle, soy tare.

辛味噌＝味噌＋豆板醤等。Miso and a chilli-bean paste on top of the chicken broth: two more fermented soy products, either of which may be barley- or wheat-fermented and neither of which has to be declared under Japanese law.

items.ja: 鶏二郎 / 鶏二郎ラーメン
items.en: Chicken Jiro — the shop’s take on the Jiro style: a mountain of boiled bean sprouts and cabbage, garlic to taste, and a very thick noodle, done with chicken instead of the usual pork
items.note: 二郎系は極太麺＝小麦、タレは醤油、野菜は茹でもやしとキャベツ。THE VEGETABLE MOUNTAIN IS NOT A VEGETARIAN DISH. A Jiro bowl is defined by the pile of boiled sprouts and cabbage on top, which is exactly the thing that makes travellers think it is the plant option — underneath it is a very thick wheat noodle in a soy tare, and here a chicken broth. The vegetables are also boiled in the same water as the noodles.

items.en: Mazesoba — no broth: thick noodles tossed with a concentrated tare and toppings at the bottom of the bowl, mixed by you
items.note: 汁なし＝タレの濃度が高い。No soup means the soy tare is more concentrated, not less. Wheat noodle. Mazesoba conventionally finishes with a raw egg yolk and minced meat, neither declared here.

items.en: Tantanmen — sesame paste and chilli oil over noodles
items.note: 担々麺は芝麻醤（ごまペースト）＋辣油＋通常は肉味噌。Sesame paste and chilli oil are the base — both plant — but a Japanese tantanmen is finished with a pork mince and its soup is normally chicken or pork stock, and this is a chicken shop. Sesame is a declarable allergen in Japan. Wheat noodle.

items.ja: 濃厚鶏つけそば ＋味玉トッピング
items.en: Dipping version of the rich chicken bowl, with an egg added
items.note: A dipping broth is a reduced broth: more concentrated chicken and more concentrated soy tare. Thicker wheat noodle.

items.en: Asahi draught — the only alcoholic drink the shop’s own page lists
items.note: ビール＝大麦麦芽。Barley malt. One of the two prices the shop publishes itself.

items.ja: ソフトドリンク（ウーロン茶・三ツ矢サイダー・ボス レインボーマウンテン）
items.en: The vending-machine soft drinks a diner recorded: Suntory oolong tea 140円, Mitsuya cider 140円, Boss Rainbow Mountain canned coffee 299円
items.note: Sealed factory drinks, so nothing in this kitchen touches them: oolong tea is leaves and water, and Mitsuya Cider is carbonated water, sugar and flavouring — both wheat-free and plant. The canned coffee is a milk coffee, so dairy. At 5am in Kabukichō these are the only things here a coeliac can have.
